title: Gideon in the winepress (Judges 6:11–16)
hookLine: hiding while threshing wheat, the least of his family is called mighty man of valor

cards: A man is threshing wheat in a winepress. That's an odd place for it. A winepress is a pit for treading grapes, and he's down inside it, beating out grain where nobody passing by can see.
The text gives the reason: "to hide it from the Midianites." Raiders have been sweeping in when the crops come up, and Israel has taken to dens and caves in the mountains. His name is Gideon.
While he crouches in that pit, the angel of the LORD sits down under an oak nearby and greets him with words that, in that moment, sound almost absurd.

teach.h: MIGHTY MAN OF VALOR, IN A HOLE.
teach.b: In the King James Bible: "The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour." To a man hiding in a hole. Gideon doesn't take the compliment.

teach.h: WHY THEN IS ALL THIS BEFALLEN US?
teach.b: He argues, and his first argument is about God, not himself: "Oh my Lord, if the LORD be with us, why then is all this befallen us?" Where, he asks, are the miracles our fathers told us about?

It's a raw question, and the text lets it stand. What he gets back isn't an explanation. It's a job: "Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee?"

teach.h: I AM THE LEAST IN MY FATHER'S HOUSE.
teach.b: So Gideon tries a second argument, about himself: "Oh my Lord, wherewith shall I save Israel? behold, my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house." He's telling the truth as he sees it.
And the reply doesn't argue. It doesn't say you're stronger than you think. It says: "Surely I will be with thee."

teach.h: THE NAME COMES BEFORE THE COURAGE.
teach.b: The name comes first. Gideon is called mighty man of valor before he has done one brave thing. Some readers hear God seeing what Gideon will become.
Others hear a name he can grow into only because God goes with him. Either way, the word arrives before the evidence. And Gideon still isn't convinced.
He asks for a sign, and later for more: a fleece left out overnight, wet and then dry. The Bible doesn't hide his doubting. It keeps him in the story anyway.

how: Some Christians turn to Gideon's call when they feel too small for a task, and some preachers use the greeting 'mighty man of valour' to speak about God naming people for what they can become.

games.q: you're Gideon, hiding in a winepress. a stranger says: the LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valor. what do you say?
o: if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us?
games.why: he asks the hard question first, then says he's the least in his father's house. the answer: "Surely I will be with thee."

practice: Bring back something kind someone once said about you that you waved away: you're a good friend, you're brave, you're good at this.

Notice what rises up to argue with it, the way Gideon argued, and don't argue back or force yourself to agree; just let the words stay in the room while you breathe. If you pray, let God hear the argument too, as Gideon did.

wordCard.voice: Gideon. The man hiding grain in a winepress, called mighty man of valor before he had done anything brave.

carryVoice: Your line: you, mighty? In this story, the name comes before the courage. See you tomorrow.
